resources.title: The archaeological network
resources.description: Comprehensive archaeological mapping of settlement and water-management features across Greater Angkor.
resources.supports: Locate channels, reservoirs and embankments; establish the spatial foundation of a reconstructed network.
resources.limitation: We have the published map and paper, not the original georeferenced GIS layers.

resources.title: How the water system developed
resources.description: A provisional archaeological reconstruction of successive changes to Angkor’s water-management system.
resources.supports: Choose a historical configuration and interpret the function and chronology of connections.
resources.limitation: A developmental interpretation rather than a calibrated hydraulic simulation.

resources.title: Landscape beneath the canopy
resources.description: Airborne LiDAR reveals channels, ponds, embankments and urban features obscured by vegetation.
resources.supports: Guide extraction of surviving hydraulic geometry from high-resolution terrain.
resources.limitation: The manuscript is local; the original georeferenced terrain and point clouds are not.

resources.title: Angkor Wat’s local landscape
resources.description: LiDAR, archives and ground investigation reinterpret the temple enclosure and its surrounding landscape.
resources.supports: Constrain local waterways and distinguish historical features from later modifications.
resources.limitation: The present northeastern moat inlet dates to 1916; modern connectivity cannot simply represent medieval conditions.

resources.title: Estimating water storage
resources.description: Estimates reservoir and moat capacities using LiDAR elevation ranges and area–depth regressions.
resources.supports: Provide initial storage estimates and a published method for filling gaps in terrain coverage.
resources.limitation: Storage proxies are not surveyed bathymetry or operational stage–storage curves. Main analysis excludes the civic-ceremonial core.

resources.title: Cascading failure in the network
resources.description: A 617-node, 1,013-edge network explores how erosion and sedimentation can concentrate flow and disrupt distribution.
resources.supports: Define diversion, flow-starvation and coupled erosion–sedimentation failure scenarios.
resources.limitation: Normalized flows and capacity updates do not supply historical volumes, travel times or bacterial concentrations.

resources.title: Hydrology and channel incision
resources.description: Examines modified catchments, sediment transport and a mathematical reconstruction of channel incision.
resources.supports: Constrain alternative bed profiles and understand changes to the regional drainage system.
resources.limitation: The channel-evolution model is described in the paper; runnable code and inputs were not located.

resources.title: The operational Hydra model
resources.description: Documents a detailed hydraulic model built from topographic surveys and monitoring, calibrated in Hydra (Hydratec).
resources.supports: Identify the most promising source of existing hydraulic geometry, storage and calibration data.
resources.limitation: Only documentation is acquired. Native project files, geometry exports and calibration performance remain unavailable.

resources.title: The hydraulic city of Angkor
resources.description: A complete symposium volume on hydraulic infrastructure and Angkor Wat, including Hang Peou’s water-management chapter.
resources.supports: Trace archaeological interpretations, restoration history and the institutional context of SDGERA.
resources.limitation: A published volume, not a downloadable hydraulic project. Modern restoration must be distinguished from historical conditions.

resources.title: Restoring the ancient system
resources.description: Describes traditional water knowledge, hydraulic structures and rehabilitation of reservoirs and supply channels.
resources.supports: Identify operational knowledge, storage figures and documented changes during restoration.
resources.limitation: Restored inlets and canal dimensions can differ from ancient arrangements. The PDF is scanned.

resources.title: A hydraulic failure reconstruction
resources.description: Combines archaeological evidence, terrain and hydraulic modelling to investigate reservoir and embankment failure at Koh Ker.
resources.supports: Provide a methodological precedent for archaeological HEC-RAS reconstruction and failure analysis.
resources.limitation: A different site. The paper is local; the HEC-RAS project is not.

resources.title: Learning to extract archaeological features
resources.description: Introduces a LiDAR-derived benchmark and methods for identifying archaeological features, including hydrological features.
resources.supports: Evaluate methods for assisted extraction of water-management features.
resources.limitation: The paper does not provide an unrestricted georeferenced terrain dataset.

resources.title: Archaeoscape source code
resources.description: Pinned source code for reproducing archaeological feature-segmentation experiments; includes configuration and training workflows.
resources.supports: Develop an extraction workflow when appropriate terrain and annotations become available.
resources.limitation: Not a hydraulic model. Trained Archaeoscape checkpoints are listed as coming soon. Code has not been installed or executed.

resources.title: Failure-model equations and rules
resources.description: Defines initialization, perturbations, capacity updates, the damage metric and generic-network experiments.
resources.supports: Reproduce the published conceptual failure mechanism and audit its assumptions.
resources.limitation: Equations and illustrations do not substitute for the original graph or a dimensional hydraulic model.

resources.title: Provisioning study supplement
resources.description: Supporting information accompanying the agricultural-economy and water-storage study.
resources.supports: Review the study’s supplementary evidence alongside the manuscript.
resources.limitation: This document does not replace the underlying tDAR data tables or the LiDAR terrain.

needs.title: Georeferenced terrain and archaeological GIS
needs.owner: APSARA Documentation Centre + EFEO Siem Reap
needs.description: Absolute-elevation bare-earth DTM, channel and embankment vectors, reservoir polygons, and original feature IDs.
needs.why: Recover cross-sections, bed slopes, basin geometry and physically meaningful connections.
needs.request: Start with a coverage index and a pilot-area GeoTIFF/GeoPackage. Include horizontal and vertical datums, acquisition dates, accuracy, phase assignments and restoration history.

needs.title: Hydra project and hydraulic geometry
needs.description: Native project plus neutral exports of cross-sections, structures, storage curves and hydraulic connections.
needs.why: Reuse surveyed geometry and understand existing flow routing before rebuilding it.
needs.request: Ask for the model inventory, coverage, software version, a sample export and one complete runnable scenario. Request gate rules and calibration documentation.

needs.title: Penny’s original graph and code
needs.description: Node and edge tables, coordinates, original GIS layers, width classes and simulation implementation.
needs.why: Connect published failure scenarios to archaeological features and dimensional geometry.
needs.request: Request stable feature IDs, source-map lineage, graph conversion rules and the exact model version used in the paper.

needs.title: Water levels, inflows and calibration observations
needs.description: Inflow hydrographs, rainfall, downstream water levels, discharge measurements and operating records.
needs.why: Geometry needs a water balance to produce water volumes, travel times and dilution under wet, dry and failure conditions.
needs.request: Request time series with units, time zones, quality flags, station coordinates and a representative calibration event. Historical forcing will require separate scenarios.

needs.title: Historical beds and control elevations
needs.description: Cores, excavation sections, old surveys and evidence for infilling, incision, dredging and inlet changes.
needs.why: Reconstruct a chosen medieval time slice rather than accidentally model the modern restored landscape.
needs.request: Prioritize pilot-area original beds, sill elevations and dated changes. Preserve alternative reconstructions where evidence is uncertain.

needs.title: Organism, sources and fate parameters
needs.description: Target bacterium, source locations and loads, inactivation, attachment, sediment exchange and any justified growth.
needs.why: Distinguish bacteria per litre, transported load and sediment-associated storage.
needs.request: Choose the organism and habitat first. Build a conservative tracer baseline before organism-specific processes; propagate uncertain parameters.

needs.title: Underlying storage and community tables
needs.description: Original feature tables underlying published storage estimates and archaeological associations.
needs.why: Use published estimates as checks and priors for reconstructed storage.
needs.request: Try authorized browser access or request the relevant tables from the authors; the automated tDAR endpoint returned HTTP 403.

needs.title: Archaeoscape terrain and annotations
needs.description: Credentialed feature-extraction benchmark; its release has no georeferencing and prohibits attempts to locate the data.
needs.why: Useful for generic segmentation research, not direct spatial alignment with Penny’s network under the published licence.
needs.request: For this reconstruction, seek separately authorized georeferenced data. No benchmark registration or agreement has been submitted.

needs.title: Related model files and missing paper
needs.description: Siem Reap incision model, Koh Ker HEC-RAS project, and Hanus & Evans’s pond-extraction PDF.
needs.why: Provide methods and comparison cases; none substitutes for the target network geometry.
needs.request: Request runnable model inputs where possible. Hanus & Evans citation metadata is local, but PDF endpoints returned HTTP 403.
